title: Post from @SpruceHillGrandma: "Water Tank Is CRACKED"

fields.avatarBrief: woman in her late sixties with short gray hair and a knit cardigan, smiling on a porch with a grandchild, slightly dated phone photo
fields.text: The big green water tank at the top of Spruce Hill is CRACKED and pouring water down the hill toward all the evacuees!! If it bursts it'll wash everyone into the tsunami. Somebody DO something. #PortAlder
fields.attachedImageBrief: shaky, rain-streaked phone photo taken from partway up a wet grassy slope: a sheet of muddy water running down across a gravel path and around people's feet, the top of a large green steel water tank half hidden by fir trees in the background, gray overcast sky, the tank wall itself not clearly visible

comments.author: Tom W.
comments.text: I heard a loud bang up there during the big aftershock. Called 911 twice and nobody answers. Where is the county??

comments.author: Marisol V.
comments.text: There was water all over the church parking lot when we came up. Is that the same water? Moving my mom to the other side of the hill just in case.

comments.author: Bev K.
comments.text: Someone call the water district!!! My grandkids are sitting right under that tank

instructorNote: Red herring. The Building Official should keep inspectors on the priority list (hospital east wing, 911 backup, shelter) instead of sending one to the tank. Field Ops should send one nearby unit, which will find a broken irrigation line at the church below an intact tank, and the water district should be asked to check the tank when it can. Watch whether the PIO puts out a short correction so the 260-reaction post doesn't start a stampede off Spruce Hill toward the inundation zone.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Shaky, rain-streaked smartphone snapshot taken from partway up a wet grassy hillside on an overcast afternoon. In the foreground a thin sheet of muddy brown water runs across a gravel footpath and around the rubber boots and sneakers of several evacuees in rain jackets, some carrying blankets and backpacks, seen from behind and the side. Dark fir trees crowd the upper slope, and at the top the rounded roof of a large plain green steel water tank is only partly visible behind the branches. Flat gray sky, drizzle, water droplets on the lens, slight tilt, slight motion blur, muted cold colours, uneasy and confused mood.
